name: Belize
summary_text: Belize demands real caution. The Court of Appeal struck down the sodomy law in 2016 (Orozco v AG) — the Caribbean's first decriminalisation ruling; Belize has an organised community (UNIBAM) and anti-discrimination employment protection. No LGR; gang violence in Belize City is a general risk.

sources.claim_summary: NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 403); the underlying Human Dignity Trust page documents constitutional challenges to laws criminalising same-sex activity across the Eastern Caribbean, including Belize (the 2016 Orozco ruling decriminalised same-sex conduct in Belize).

sources.title: Antigua and Barbuda: High Court Decriminalizes Gay Sex | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: NOTE: This HRW article is about Antigua and Barbuda's 2022 decriminalisation ruling, not Belize specifically; included as Eastern Caribbean regional context.

sources.title: Belize turnaround on gay rights: 'Unbelievable!'
sources.claim_summary: Erasing 76 Crimes (Nov 2018): Belize's turnaround on gay rights - accepted 15 of 17 SOGI recommendations at its UPR (first CARICOM country to accept that many), after decriminalising in 2016; activist Caleb Orozco describes the 180-degree turn in the state's SOGI position.

sources.title: Belize's top court strikes down sodomy law
sources.claim_summary: Washington Blade (Aug 2016): Belize's top court strikes down the sodomy law.

sources.title: Is Belize Gay-Friendly? An Overview | www.centralamerica.com
sources.claim_summary: Central America living guide (April 2019): 'Is Belize gay-friendly?' - local writer on improving conditions; the 2016 decriminalisation (first former British Caribbean colony to overturn its anti-sodomy law); tourism has long been gay-friendly (1998 gay cruise protests vs 2009 welcomed lesbian cruise); Caleb Orozco's constitutional challenge and UNIBAM's work.

sources.title: Belize challenge to anti-gay law, 140 characters at a time
sources.claim_summary: Erasing 76 Crimes (May 2013): courtroom coverage of the Orozco constitutional challenge to Section 53 (the anti-sodomy law) - live-tweeted dispatches from psychologist Asa DeMatteo describing the arguments on constitutional fundamental rights versus church intervenors.
